{{Top|leg}}
'''Intellex''' was a series of [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]] used in [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]].<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|II|106|Intellex}}</ref> The series included the [[Intellex ship-configuration computer]],<ref name="The Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> [[Intellex II]], [[Intellex III]], [[Intellex IV/Legends|Intellex IV]], [[Intellex V/Legends|Intellex V]], and [[Intellex VI]].<ref name="TCSWE" />

== History ==
[[Intellex ship-configuration computer|Intellex]] was a powerful [[Computer/Legends|computer]] configuration system that was conceived by [[Industrial Intelligence/Legends|Industrial Intelligence]]. When [[Automata Galactica/Legends|Automaton Galactica]] bought out Industrial Intelligence, the higher executives at Industrial Intelligence sealed their data concerning top-secret projects, like the Intellex, in an encrypted memory vault. Automaton Galactica eventually managed to [[Slicer/Legends|slice]] some files and found the Intellex. Intellex was originally designed to be an advisory "housekeeping" system for [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. It was small, capable of sorting incredible amounts of information, and featured a system that allowed it to adapt and improve existing computer configurations. This original system held 200 starship configurations and could perform 7,000 [[MPF]] operations a second.<ref name=":0">{{JournalCite|7|The History of R-Series Astromech Droids}}</ref> 

As a dedicated [[Droid/Legends|droid]] hardware manufacturer, Automata Galactica took the Intellex system and implanted it into a prototype [[Astromech droid/Legends|maintenance droid]] called the [[P2-series astromech droid|P2]]. The P2's first tests aboard the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic's]] shipping fleet proved positive. [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] planned to bring the P2 into the public market after modifying its Intellex computer. The [[Intellex II]] was created to facilitate the droid's new database system. This new system was capable of handling new and different starship types, including dedicated [[Capital ship/Legends|capital warships]]. [[Technician/Legends|Technicians]] even included a primitive [[Navigation computer/Legends|nav computer]] program that could calculate one [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump if given enough time and input.<ref name=":0" /> 

Before the P2 and its Intellex II could reach the final development stage, the former executives of Industrial Intelligence sued Industrial Automaton for using their Intellex system. Given the state of the Republic's bureaucracy, it took [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] before the case ever went to trial. Production froze during this time and Industrial Automaton lost millions of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. When Industrial Intelligence realized the case would bring unwanted attention to their secret datafile vault and business practices, they dropped the case. The legal hassle and bad publicity forces Industrial Automaton to drop the P2 and the Intellex II.<ref name=":0" />

Industrial Automaton attempted to recover as many losses as they could by releasing the [[R1-series astromech droid/Legends|R1-series astromech]]. The R1 was implanted with the new [[Intellex III]] which was capable of handling large transports and capital warships. It featured 500 starship designs and operated at a speed of 10,000 MPF. The new computer was also capable of calculating a single jump in unprecedented time.<ref name=":0" /> 

The popularity of the R1 and its Intellex III on warships and large commercial freighters led to the development of the [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech]] and further advances in the Intellex computer. The R2 and its [[Intellex IV/Legends|Intellex IV]] held 700 starship designs and an improved hyperjump coordinate cache that could hold up to 10 jumps in [[RAM]]. It was also designed with a focus on [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] interface.<ref name=":0" /> 

IA rode the wave of success of the R2-series to further improve the Intellex computer for higher performance levels. The [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3-series astromech]] and its [[Intellex V/Legends|Intellex V]] were dedicated to capital warship and [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] service, with added gunnery repair and security features. The R3 was given a transparent dome to show off the new Intellex V.<ref name=":0" /> 

In response to price complaints of the R2-series and the elitist image that was unintentional created for the R3-series, IA began to develop the cheaper [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4-series]] for the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] urban market. The R4's [[Intellex IV/Legends|Intellex VI]] featured [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] designs and starship configurations, and could only hold one jump in its RAM.<ref name=":0" />

The [[R5-series astromech droid|R5-series]] was advertised as an economy model of the R2, but it failed as an astromech because its computer could only hold one jump in its RAM.<ref name=":0" /> 

The [[R6-series astromech droid|R6-series]] was released by IA as a "new beginning" for consumer droids under the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. It released with incredible processing ability, and was able to hold 12 jumps in its RAM.<ref name=":0" /> 

The [[R7-series astromech droid|R7-series]] was commissioned by the New Republic to serve in new starfighter designs constructed by [[FreiTek Incorporated/Legends|FreiTek Incorporated]], specifically the [[E-7 E-wing multi-role starfighter|E-wing starfighter]]. IA engineers replaced the traditional Intellex computer with a dedicated [[FreiTek computer system]], allowing the R7 to obtain a higher counterpart interactivity ratio than the old Intellex configuration ever achieved.<ref name=":0" />
